sources.headline: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
sources.text: A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.Ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024. Iran's laws ban public performances by women and require them to wear headscarves and modest clothing.This June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material", which they had denied.In addition to being sentenced to 74 lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years.At the end of September, an appeals court in Qom rejected the defendants' appeal and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said.There was widespread condemnation of the sentences from other Iranian artists and human rights activists, who warned that flogging constituted cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violated the international prohibition on torture.On Monday, one of the defendants' lawyers told the BBC that Ahmadi and four of her male co-defendants had been flogged at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom."We did everything in our power to have the verdict overturned, or at least to secure a reduction in the sentence or a suspension, but it didn't work out," he said."The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately."Pro-reform daily Etemad cited another defence lawyer, Mostafa Nili, as identifying the four men flogged alongside Ahmadi as Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari."Parastoo Ahmadi's flogging for singing and dressing as she chooses is a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights and a chilling demonstration of the Iranian authorities' determination to suppress women's freedoms and to violently punish anyone who dares to challenge their discriminatory laws and policies," said Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI).Under Iranian law, which is based on the country's interpretation of Sharia, women and girls above the age of puberty must cover their hair with a hijab and wear long, loose-fitting clothing to disguise their figures.In 2022, protests swept across the Islamic Republic following the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman who was detained by morality police in Tehran in September that year for allegedly wearing her hijab "improperly".Women burnt their headscarves or waved them in the air at the nationwide demonstrations against the clerical establishment, during which hundreds of people were killed in a crackdown by security forces.Since then, many women and girls have stopped covering their hair in public altogether in open defiance of the dress code. Authorities have responded with periodic waves of arrests, warnings, business closures and other measures.In January this year, thousands of people were killed and tens of thousands were arrested when security forces crushed another wave of mass anti-establishment protests, this time sparked by the country's economic crisis.Since the start of Iran's war with the US and Israel in late February, authorities have intensified their use of the death penalty against protesters.According to the Norway-based group Iran Human Rights, at least 39 men convicted over January's protests and two convicted over the 2022 unrest have been executed, along with 16 people allegedly affiliated with banned opposition groups and 17 others convicted of espionage or collaborating with foreign states.Another 121 protesters detained in January, including six women and five juvenile offenders, have been sentenced to death and are at imminent risk of execution, it says.

sources.text: Parastoo Ahmadi sang without wearing the mandatory veil in a virtual concert in 2024 that spread quickly online and drew the ire of the Islamic republic authorities.

UN slams Iran after it flogs singer for performing without veil

The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, local media reported, citing Ahmadi's lawyer.

Issued on: 24/11/2026 - 21:53
Modified: 24/11/2026 - 21:54

FRANCE 24
Iranian authorities carried out a sentence of 74 lashes today, November 23, 2026, against Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four musicians, according to their lawyer Mostafa Nili. © Image taken from social media

The United Nations branded the lashing of a prominent Iranian singer and her production team as "abhorrent" and said Tehran must eradicate flogging.

Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team were lashed 74 times each on Monday after a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, according to local media reports citing her lawyer.

All the musicians wore black, with Ahmadi dressed in a long, strappy gown and wearing deep red lipstick, in a country where women are banned from singing in public. They are also required to dress modestly and wear the headscarf.

Read moreIran's courts order US to pay $290 billion in damages

Ahmadi, 29, was sentenced in June to the lashes alongside the others, for the concert posted online in December 2024.

"The flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four male members of her team – following a concert she gave without wearing headcover – is abhorrent," UN rights chief Volker Turk said on X.

"Flogging is a form of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment, absolutely prohibited under international law in all circumstances.

"Iran must abstain from carrying out other flogging sentences and eradicate this practice from its laws."

Increasing numbers of Iranian women are appearing without hijab, especially since protests erupted following the death in custody of a woman named Mahsa Amini in September 2022. She had been arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.

(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

sources.headline: Iranian women praise singer lashed for not wearing a hijab
sources.text:
By
Kamal Afzali,
Updated on: November 24, 2026 / 12:40 PM EST
/ CBS News
Add CBS News on Google
Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed 74 times on Monday after being convicted of the crime of "outraging public decency" for performing without the head covering that is mandatory for women in the country. Ahmadi was dealt the corporal punishment for her chosen attire during a livestreamed concert in 2024, according to her attorney, who was quoted by the reformist Iranian newspaper Etemad on Monday. But Iranian women who spoke with CBS News on Tuesday said she was punished not for breaking the rule, but for daring to publicly defy the country's repressive regime — defiance that has made her "a symbol of resistance." Ahmadi's lawyer told Etemad that the singer and four members of her production team presented themselves to provincial authorities in the holy city of Qom, as required after their sentences were upheld in September by a local criminal court.
Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed 74 times by Iranian authorities for "outraging public decency" by singing without her hair covered, as required by Iranian dress code rules for women, in a livestreamed 2024 concert.
Parastoo Ahmadi/YouTube
The court in Qom upheld the convictions for "outraging public decency," citing "immoral" content posted online during Ahmadi's performance in December 2024, which went viral in Iran.In addition to the 74 lashes, Ahmadi and eight members of her team were also sentenced to a two-year ban on travel out of the country and a two-year ban on all "artistic activity." Ahmadi performed her concert in the Dayr-Gachin Caravanserai, an ancient site along the Silk Road route in Iran. It included themes of nationalism and popular uprising, and saw her openly flout both the Islamic Republic's dress code and a long-standing ban on women singing in public."I feel as though I have been flogged"Ahmadi's punishment has reverberated across the country as her performance did two years ago.
"When it comes to her flogging, I feel deep pain," Marjan, a 41-year-old optician from Karaj, a city northwest of Tehran, told CBS News on Tuesday. "I feel as though I have been flogged for doing what I want.""This is something which is much deeper than just sympathy or solidarity," she said. "We Iranian women identify with her in a deeper psychological sense."Marjan, who declined to give her full name, called Ahmadi "a symbol of resistance." "She was an icon when she performed in that concert, and now, after she received those lashes. Both are acts of resistance," said Marjan, who spoke with CBS News over the phone. "The regime is not afraid of women who sing, they are afraid of people who courageously carry out that which they prohibit."
This "is not the punishment of an artist, it is the punishment of a person who made use of their most fundamental rights of freedom of speech and creative expression," agreed Tehran resident Thoraya, 32."No state has ownership over the voices of their citizens. Singing is not a crime," she told CBS News, also in a phone interview. "No state power can precondition artistic expression on political obedience. I feel solidarity with Parastoo, but it's human solidarity first and foremost, not political.""I'm not taking her place or speaking for her," she said, "but her right to wear what she wants, pursue her artistic life, is something I see as my right, too."

Iran
Protest

sources.headline: Iran flogs singer Parastoo Ahmadi for performing without headscarf
sources.text: Ahmadi and four production team members also face two-year bans on travel and artistic activity.Iran has flogged a singer and her production team after they were convicted of “offending public decency”, according to local media.The sentence of 74 lashes handed down to Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team was carried out in the city of Qom on Monday, the singer’s lawyer Mostafa Nili told the Emtedad news website.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Tajikistan moves to leave ICC amid US push against courtlist 2 of 4Danish top court’s ‘ghetto law’ ruling supports hardline immigration policylist 3 of 4India pledges $1.6bn in flood relief for Nepal as Balendra Shah visits Modilist 4 of 4What Russian warship did Ukraine just sink?end of listA court in the city had sentenced the quintet in June. They were convicted of “producing and publishing obscene and immoral content online” over a video showing Ahmadi performing without wearing the mandatory hijab alongside male musicians.The video was posted on YouTube in December 2024. In addition to the flogging, the five were banned for two years from taking part in artistic and musical activities and leaving Iran.Western governments and human rights groups have condemned flogging as a form of torture that violates international law.Iran rejects criticism of its human rights record and says Western countries should address abuses of their own.Iran’s mandatory hijab rules became a focal point of protests in 2022 after Mahsa Amini, a Kurdish Iranian woman, died in custody following her arrest for allegedly violating the dress code.More women have since defied the rules in Tehran and elsewhere in Iran, while authorities have enforced them more selectively.
